---
title: "Plots with ggplot2 and tmap"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

`geom_basemap()` ({ggplot2}) and `tm_basemap()` ({tmap}) add a basemap
under your data. They render when the plot is drawn, for the panel's extent
and at the output device's resolution: on screen, in this page, or in
`ggsave(dpi = 300)` and `tmap_save(dpi = 300)`, labels stay sharp and
the right size. Both take the arguments of `basemap()`'s renderers (`labels`,
`features`, `layers`, `alpha`, ...) and credit the provider in the corner.

```{r}
library(tmap)        # before basemapper: basemapper's tm_basemap() replaces tmap's
library(basemapper)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
```

## ggplot2

```{r ggplot-choropleth}
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron") +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = SID79 / BIR79 * 1000), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_distiller("SIDS per 1,000\nbirths, 1979", palette = "OrRd", direction = 1) +
  theme_void()
```

### Projected data

The basemap is rendered in Web Mercator and warped to the plot's coordinate
system, so data in any CRS works. Here North Carolina's state plane
(EPSG:32119), with the counties' centroids:

```{r ggplot-projected}
nc_sp <- st_transform(nc, 32119)
centroids <- st_centroid(nc_sp)

ggplot(nc_sp) +
  geom_basemap("Esri.WorldTopoMap") +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = centroids, aes(size = BIR74), colour = "#D96E34", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size_area("Births, 1974", max_size = 6) +
  theme_void()
```

### A quieter basemap

For a data map, a basemap often reads better without its labels, faded, or
with only some of its features (see [Stacking, labels and
features](layers.html)):

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels = FALSE, features = c("-roads", "-rail"), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = NWBIR74 / BIR74), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c("Share of births,\nnon-white, 1974", labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_void()
```

### Zooming in

The basemap follows the panel, so `coord_sf()` limits zoom it in, with
detail to match:

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap("Esri.WorldImagery") +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "yellow", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = NAME), colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-76.9, -75.4), ylim = c(35.0, 36.0)) +
  theme_void()
```

### Credits

The credit line is on by default. `attribution = FALSE` turns it off;
`get_attribution()` returns the text, for a caption:

```{r}
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", attribution = FALSE) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(caption = get_attribution("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas")) +
  theme_void()
```

## tmap

`tm_basemap()` is a {tmap} v4 layer; it takes its extent from the map's
shapes. tmap has a `tm_basemap()` of its own, so attach tmap before
basemapper (or call `basemapper::tm_basemap()`):

```{r}
tm_shape(nc) +
  tm_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron") +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "BIR79", fill_alpha = 0.75, col = "white", lwd = 0.5,
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.blues"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Births, 1979")
  )
```

Raster and vector basemaps, stacks, labels and features work the same way;
here shaded relief under a vector basemap's labels:

```{r tmap-relief}
relief <- c("Esri.WorldShadedRelief", basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels = "only"))

tm_shape(nc_sp) +
  tm_basemap(relief) +
  tm_borders(col = "grey20", lwd = 0.6) +
  tm_dots(size = "BIR74", fill = "#D96E34", fill_alpha = 0.7, size.legend = tm_legend("Births, 1974"))
```
